$comment: Board3's real design rules. This file exists because KiCad's EasyEDA Pro
importer does NOT translate design rules -- it brings geometry, nets and the
schematic faithfully, then writes KiCad's stock factory defaults into the
That substitution is silent and expensive. Measured against those invented
rules, an untouched Board3 reports 544 DRC violations, 503 of them clearance
-- every one a false positive, all sitting in a 0.117-0.197 mm band just under
a 0.2 mm rule the board was never drawn to. Against the real rules below the
same board reports 41. EasyEDA's own DRC was right all along.
Anyone migrating a board here who trusts the imported .kicad_pro will chase
hundreds of phantom violations and route to constraints their fab never agreed

$notes.track_width: 0.254 mm (10 mil) is what every track on Board3 actually is, so it is the design's working width rather than the process floor. The 0.1016 mm minimum is JLC's standard limit; 0.09 mm (3.5 mil) is reachable on their ADVANCED process at extra cost, which is what an autorouter necks down to at fine-pitch pads if it is not constrained.
$notes.annular_ring: JLC wants 0.15 mm minimum, 0.2 mm preferred. Not expressible as a single KiCad rule key; watch the annular_width violation class instead.

differential_pairs.$resolved: 2026-07-27. Resolved by MEASUREMENT of the board rather than recovery from EasyEDA, because the measurement made recovery moot: ALL 2435 tracks on Board3 are 0.254 mm. There is exactly one track width on this board and no differential-pair geometry was ever applied in copper. Whatever the EasyEDA net-class panel said, it did not shape this board -- so these are decisions to make, not values to recover. The '10mm' memory is 10 mil = 0.254 mm, i.e. the board-wide default, which is consistent with no pair-specific rule having reached copper.
differential_pairs.$stackup_assumption: The importer carried NO stackup block, so impedance is computed against JLCPCB's standard 4-layer 1.6 mm stackup (JLC04161H-7628): Top 1oz / prepreg 7628 0.2104 mm Er~4.4 / Inner1 / core 1.065 mm / Inner2 / prepreg 0.2104 mm / Bottom 1oz. Figures below are closed-form edge-coupled microstrip for a top-layer pair over a SOLID Inner1 ground. CONFIRM against JLCPCB's own impedance calculator before fabrication, and confirm the reference plane is actually continuous under each pair -- an impedance number over a split plane is fiction.
differential_pairs.$as_drawn: 0.254 mm trace over 0.2104 mm prepreg gives Zo ~60 ohm single-ended. At the board's 0.254 mm spacing that is Zdiff ~102 ohm -- inside USB's 90 ohm +/-15% window (76.5-103.5) but sitting at its top edge, and low for CAN's 120 ohm.

USB.note: Keep the board-wide 0.254 mm width and TIGHTEN THE GAP to 0.15 mm. This is the minimal-change option: it preserves the single-width virtue of the board, and it matches the lost action item's wording -- 'narrow it' meant narrow the gap, not the trace. Narrowing the TRACE would raise impedance away from 90 ohm, which is the trap in that note. Alternative if a 0.15 mm gap is uncomfortable: 0.30 mm width with 0.21 mm gap, also ~90 ohm.

CAN.computed_zdiff_ohm: 114 at 0.5 mm gap, 118 at 0.75 mm gap
CAN.note: CAN wants the OPPOSITE treatment to USB: loosely coupled. With 0.254 mm traces, Zdiff asymptotically approaches 2*Zo = ~120 ohm as the gap grows, so a WIDE gap (>=0.5 mm) is what reaches 120 ohm. Tightening a CAN pair the way you tighten USB drives it away from target. In practice this matters little at 1 Mbps over 23-25 mm of track -- symmetry, equal via counts and the split termination dominate -- so treat the gap as a target, not a constraint to contort the layout around.
